---
title: "return without parentheses does not leave the function"
ref: FUN-15
categories: [Functions]
impact: silencieux
extrait: '(function() { return; "after" })()'
reponse: '"after"'
attendu: "`NULL`: the function should stop before `log()`"
versions: "All"
source: "General R knowledge"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
safe_log <- function(x) {
  if (x <= 0) {
    return
  }
  log(x)
}
safe_log(-1)
```
:::

## Why

In R, `return` is a function. Written alone, without parentheses, it is just its name: R evaluates the symbol, gets the function, does nothing with it and moves on to the next line. The guard stops nothing, and `log(-1)` runs.

The habit comes from C, Java or JavaScript, where `return;` ends a function. R raises neither an error nor a warning about the `return` itself. Here, the only clue is the warning of `log()`, and there is none at all when the next line accepts the value.

## The remedy

Always call it: `return()` returns `NULL`, `return(value)` returns the value.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
safe_log <- function(x) {
  if (x <= 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  log(x)
}
safe_log(-1)
safe_log(exp(2))
```
:::
